### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via translatePage (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9e413215bac8a5abf058e6791cfa51cc8e821803` — the merge of head `d841d2686fd54047b5ce72724c97726a029f7c9a` into base `86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9e413215bac8a5abf058e6791cfa51cc8e821803 && git checkout 9e413215bac8a5abf058e6791cfa51cc8e821803
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34 d841d2686fd54047b5ce72724c97726a029f7c9a && git checkout -B drift-repro 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34 && git merge --no-ff d841d2686fd54047b5ce72724c97726a029f7c9a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 86f53a4b8d818706b367b3b89de0e33d92395f34` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d841d2686fd54047b5ce72724c97726a029f7c9a`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #22598 for card #22536, at the branch head above (the head the brief named; the branch has not moved). Inputs: the card body and all nine comments (triage `6089133193`, the unlock, the deferral, the claim `6092445731`, both dev reports `6092591933` and `6093422367`, the retriage ask `6092610387` and triage's answer `6092658777`, the seat's ACCEPT `6093434692`), the PR body and file list, the net diff of the head against its merge-base with `origin/main` (`99801d831f`; two commits on the branch, the fix `cdfc9efa7a` and one merge of `main`), the check-runs on the head, and objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `47b1f0bb71`, read only. The diff is 4 files, +214 / -5: `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`, its test, `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, and `.changeset/22536-record-page-header-title.md`. No governed path.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The one arm that moved in `resolvePageHeaderTitle`, and nothing else — RIGHT.** Before: `if (own === undefined || sameAuthoredText(own, authoredPageLabel)) return bundleLabel; return undefined;`. After: `if (own === undefined) return derivesFromRecord ? undefined : bundleLabel; if (sameAuthoredText(own, authoredPageLabel)) return bundleLabel; return undefined;`. The four cells of the authored-title axis: no authored title on a non-record header still takes the bundle `label`; no authored title on a record-deriving header now stays absent (the only cell that changed); an authored title restating the page `label` still takes the label's translation, the new flag not consulted; an authored title saying anything else is still kept. Step 1 (a bundle `pages.NAME.title` wins) and the early return when the bundle carries no label are byte-unchanged. `authoredLabelText` is untouched, so `title: ''` and an all-empty locale map still count as untitled, the same as before.

2. **`headerDerivesFromRecord` is exactly triage's predicate A (`6092658777`) — RIGHT.** `page.type === 'record'` read literally off the served document (no `PageSchema` default applied), `typeof page.object === 'string'` with a non-zero `page.object.length`, and `header.properties?.recordChrome !== false`. Checked against the pin: `containers.tsx:2331`–`:2332` draws the record heading only when `ctx.data && ctx.objectSchema` and `!disableRecordChrome`; `usePageAssignment.ts:139`–`:140` rejects `p.type !== 'record'` and `p.object !== objectName`; `PagePreview.tsx:186`–`:187` keys `isRecordPage` on `type === 'record'` and `recordObject` on `object`, and `:311` mounts the context only when `recordObject` is truthy (so `object: ''` is unmounted there too, matching the non-empty-string conjunct). D (any object-bound page) is not taken, as triage amended. A `page:header` with no `properties` bag at all on a record page reads as deriving (`undefined !== false`), the same as the renderer's `schema?.properties?.recordChrome === false` being false.

3. **Only `properties.recordChrome` is read — RIGHT.** The renderer reads both `schema.recordChrome` and `schema.properties.recordChrome` (`containers.tsx:1573`–`:1574`), but `PageComponentSchema` (`page.zod.ts:308`) is a `strictObject` declaring `type`, `id`, `label`, `properties` and nothing named `recordChrome`, so a parsed document never carries the bare spelling; reading it would tolerate a refused key. The dev's measured `unrecognized_keys` matches the schema as it stands.

4. **The `translatePage` call site writes no phantom key — RIGHT.** The header rebuild spreads `title` only when `headerTitle !== undefined` and returns `next` untouched when both title and subtitle resolve to `undefined`, so a record-page header with a bundle `subtitle` is served `{recordChrome: true, subtitle}` with no `title` key, and the pin that asserts `'title' in properties` is false holds on the no-subtitle path. The region root and the slot root reach the one call with `nested: false`, so both pin sets exercise the same resolution.

5. **Public surface unchanged; accept set unchanged — RIGHT.** `translatePage` and `translateMetadataDocument` keep their exported signatures (`system/index.ts` re-exports the module; `api-surface/system.json` lists `translatePage (function)` and is not in the diff). `resolvePageHeaderTitle` and `headerDerivesFromRecord` are module-private, so the added parameter is internal. `PageLike` already declares `object?: string` and an open index signature, and `PageComponentLike` already declares `properties`, so no type widened. `component.zod.ts` and `page.zod.ts` are untouched: nothing accepts more or less. The dev reports `check:generated` at 15 of 15 current at this head, and the `Spec property liveness` check-run on the head is green. What changes is one served value: an untitled record-page header no longer gains `properties.title` from the pack's `label`, in every locale whose pack carries it. That is the ruled meaning of an omitted title (`PageHeaderProps.title`, the #7702 ruling in `component.zod.ts:590`–`:604`) restored, not a surface change.

6. **The #22508 control is amended as triage directed, not overturned — RIGHT.** The fixture page `account_detail_page` carries no `type` and no `object`, so it is a non-record page as served; the pin keeps its assertions and gains only the words "on a non-record page", which is the amendment triage `6089133193` announced. Option C, which would have flipped that control, is not taken.

7. **The docs sentence states A's condition and touches no release page — RIGHT.** `translations.mdx` adds the exception beside the label-fallback sentence in the same callout, as triage `6092658777` asked. The docs-drift bot named `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx` as naming `translatePage`; it is release-owned and the diff correctly leaves it alone.

8. **The pins and the ablation reconcile — RIGHT.** Per root: two seeded-header pins (zh-CN label-only pack, en extract skeleton), one `recordChrome`-at-default pin (`{}` and `{title: ''}`), one subtitle-beside-untitled pin, equals 4; times two roots plus the `translateMetadataDocument` pin equals the 9 the ablation turned red. One control per conjunct (`type` absent; `object` absent or `''`; `recordChrome: false`) plus the other-`type` control (`list`, `app`, `home`, `utility`), and the three authored-title arms on a record page, stayed green under the ablation, which is what "nothing wider moved" needs.

9. **The modal-host gap is the accepted one — RIGHT.** `useActionModal.tsx:197`–`:210` renders any page fetched by name as modal content, and `{modalElement}` sits at `RecordDetailView.tsx:3064` inside the `RecordContextProvider` opened at `:2849`, so a non-record page shown there derives its heading from the host record while keeping the label fill. Triage accepted that gap by name; the `headerDerivesFromRecord` docblock records it.

### ② Semver level

- **Packages this diff publishes in:** `@objectstack/spec` only (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`; the test file does not ship). `content/docs` does not publish; the changeset is the entry itself.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/22536-record-page-header-title.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, carries `Clause-②: no` with no `(widening)` / `(narrowing)` arm, and describes the three-conjunct rule, the before measurement and what stays unchanged. A bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`, and no `skip-changeset` label is on the PR. **Level: patch — RIGHT.**
- **`Clause-②: no` — judged, and right.** No accept set changes (no zod file in the diff), no export is added, removed or re-signed, no type widens. The one behavioural change narrows a served fill on one class of input to the meaning the spec already ruled for it. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no` on its second line. The `Check Changeset` check-run on the head is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag from `6093422367` (deviations, `open_questions`, `out_of_scope_findings`) and the PR's Acceptance notes, answered here:

- **`open_questions` is empty in the final report.** The first report's one question (which predicate) was answered by triage `6092658777` as A, with `type` read as served; the code is that answer. Answered.
- **Deviation: only `properties.recordChrome` read.** Verified against `PageComponentSchema` (① item 3). Accepted.
- **Finding: `PageSchema` defaults `type` to `'record'` at parse (`page.zod.ts:1177`) while an unparsed registry page is served typeless and keeps the label fill.** Triage said record it, do not fix it here; the dev measured it, found no real producer (`defineStack` applies the default; in-tree plugin pages declare `type`), and the seat kept it in the Acceptance notes without a card for want of reach. The resolver and the hosts agree on a typeless document (`usePageAssignment` reads `type` literally too), so spec and renderer do not diverge on it; the seam is the registry read path, outside this card. Disposition stands. Answered, not escalated.
- **Finding: a pack's `pages.NAME.title` and `subtitle` still apply to an untitled record-page header.** That is step 1 of the order #22508 ruled: a pack `title` is the translator authoring a title in that locale on purpose, which is not the label-for-title swap the card is about. The ruling covered the label alone. Answered, not escalated.
- **Consumer suites ran at `cdfc9efa7a`, before the `main` merge.** The merge brought four commits none of which touch the translator files; after it the dev re-ran the resolver and translation tests, the spec build with `check:generated`, and the gate union. The check-runs on this head are the verdict for everything else; see the CI line below.
- **`dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally,** as the dispatch ruled out a whole-workspace build; `Build Core` on the head is green.
- **Commit trailers use AGENTS.md's model-free pair.** Not contract-bearing.
- **Reviewer finding, not blocking:** `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`, `pages` entry, still says the label stands in "only where the header authors none or restates the page label". After this PR that clause has the record-page exception. The entry's status, anchors and evidence targets are unchanged and the `Spec property liveness` check-run is green, so this is ledger prose drift, not a liveness change; the seat can fold the one-clause amendment into the next touch of that ledger. Left with the seat.
- **Governed surfaces:** none of the four paths is governed. The review is owed by the landing rule's path limb (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test), as the seat's ACCEPT corrected; this record is that review.
- **CI on the head, read at 2026-10-10T03:52Z:** 22 success, 5 skipped, 0 failed, 10 still in progress: `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`. Green already: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1/3, 2/3 and 3/3, `Check Documentation Links`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the three PR-context guards, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Nothing has failed. This verdict is on the diff and the completed checks; the landing still waits for every required context to finish green, and a red among the ten would stand over this record. GitHub reports the PR `mergeable: true` with `mergeable_state: blocked` (a draft awaiting checks); no conflict against `main` is reported.
